instructions: Heat the oven to 320°F. Cut 12 slices from the baguette, about 1/4 inch thick, on a slant.
Lay the slices on a baking sheet and brush the tops with the olive oil. Bake for 4 to 5 minutes, until golden and crisp. Transfer them to a rack to cool.
Meanwhile, put the ricotta in a bowl and whisk it hard for 1 to 2 minutes, until it's smooth and fluffy.
Spread about 2 teaspoons of ricotta on each toast. Drizzle with the honey, scatter on the thyme leaves and add a tiny pinch of salt on each.
Serve right away, so the toasts stay crisp.
method_notes: Both sources keep this to toasted bread, ricotta and honey, with thyme or lemon zest as the only extras. The lead tops it with pine nuts; those are left off here to keep it nut-free. The lead whips the ricotta in a food processor; a hand whisk does it for this small amount. The toasts keep for a day in a closed container, and the ricotta keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days, so assemble just before eating.
